question.problem:
Consider the vector $x$ and the subspace $S=\text{Span}\{{a}_{1},{a}_{2}\},$ where

$$
{a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 0 \\ 2\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ -1\end{aligned}],\,\,x=[\begin{aligned}6 \\ -1 \\ -4\end{aligned}].
$$

Find the distance between $x$ and the subspace $S$ given that the set $\{{a}_{1},{a}_{2}\}$ is orthogonal.
question.worked_solution:
Since the set $\{{a}_{1},{a}_{2}\}$ is orthogonal, the orthogonal projection of $x$ onto the subspace $S$ is given by

$$
{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x={\text{proj}}_{{a}_{1}}x+{\text{proj}}_{{a}_{2}}x.
$$

So, we first find the orthogonal projections of $x$ onto $\text{Span}\{{a}_{1}\}$ and $\text{Span}\{{a}_{2}\}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{{a}_{1}}x & =\frac{x\cdot {a}_{1}}{{a}_{1}\cdot {a}_{1}}{a}_{1}=\frac{6\cdot 2+(-1)\cdot 0+(-4)\cdot 2}{{2}^{2}+{0}^{2}+{2}^{2}}{a}_{1}=\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 0 \\ 2\end{aligned}] \\ {\text{proj}}_{{a}_{2}}x & =\frac{x\cdot {a}_{2}}{{a}_{2}\cdot {a}_{2}}{a}_{2}=\frac{6\cdot 1+(-1)\cdot 1+(-4)\cdot (-1)}{{1}^{2}+{1}^{2}+(-1)^{2}}{a}_{2}=3[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ -1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have that

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x & ={\text{proj}}_{{a}_{1}}x+{\text{proj}}_{{a}_{2}}x \\  & =\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 0 \\ 2\end{aligned}]+3[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 3 \\ -2\end{aligned}]=\overset{^}{x}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the distance between $x$ and the subspace $S$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}d(x,\overset{^}{x}) & =‖x-\overset{^}{x}‖ \\  & =\sqrt{({x}_{1}-{\overset{^}{x}}_{1})^{2}+({x}_{2}-{\overset{^}{x}}_{2})^{2}+({x}_{3}-{\overset{^}{x}}_{3})^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{{(6-4)}^{2}+{(-1-3)}^{2}+{(-4-(-2))}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{4+16+4} \\  & =2\sqrt{6}.\end{aligned}
$$
